name: file-permissions
description: Credential, cron, auth and banner file/dir permissions (CIS 6.1 / 5.1).  Absent keys/paths SKIP, never false-fail.

rules.title: /etc/security/opasswd not overly permissive
rules.rationale: opasswd stores old password hashes for reuse checks — same offline-cracking risk as shadow.

rules.title: /etc/login.defs not overly permissive
rules.rationale: login.defs sets password/UID policy; a writable copy lets a user relax it.

rules.title: /etc/ssh/ssh_config not overly permissive
rules.rationale: A writable client config can be used to weaken outbound SSH (e.g. disable host-key checks).

rules.title: /etc/sudoers not overly permissive
rules.rationale: A writable sudoers file is a direct, unaudited path to root.

rules.title: /etc/sudoers.d not overly permissive
rules.rationale: A writable sudoers.d drop-in directory is the same root path by another door.

rules.title: /etc/cron.hourly not overly permissive
rules.rationale: Writable cron dir = scheduled root code execution.

rules.title: /etc/cron.daily not overly permissive
rules.rationale: Writable cron dir = scheduled root code execution.

rules.title: /etc/cron.weekly not overly permissive
rules.rationale: Writable cron dir = scheduled root code execution.

rules.title: /etc/cron.monthly not overly permissive
rules.rationale: Writable cron dir = scheduled root code execution.

rules.title: /etc/cron.allow not overly permissive
rules.rationale: cron.allow controls who may schedule jobs; keep it tight.

rules.title: /etc/cron.deny not overly permissive
rules.rationale: cron.deny is part of the same access decision.

rules.title: /etc/at.allow not overly permissive
rules.rationale: at.allow controls who may schedule 'at' jobs.

rules.title: /etc/at.deny not overly permissive
rules.rationale: at.deny is part of the same access decision.

rules.title: /etc/hosts.allow not overly permissive
rules.rationale: tcpwrappers policy file — shouldn't be world-writable.

rules.title: /etc/hosts.deny not overly permissive
rules.rationale: tcpwrappers deny file — shouldn't be world-writable.

rules.title: /etc/motd not overly permissive
rules.rationale: A writable login banner can be abused for social-engineering.

rules.title: /etc/issue not overly permissive
rules.rationale: A writable console banner can be abused likewise.

rules.title: /etc/issue.net not overly permissive
rules.rationale: A writable network banner can be abused likewise.

rules.title: /boot/grub2/grub.cfg not overly permissive
rules.rationale: GRUB2 config leaks boot parameters and can hide a boot password; keep it root-only.
